use: a data story from a pasted CSV
request: Here's a CSV I pulled from Our World in Data. Make a short data story from it: how much longer people live now than in 1900.

material.name: life_expectancy.csv
material.about: world life expectancy at birth, years
material.text:
year,life_expectancy
1900,32
1950,46
2000,66
2021,71
# note: child mortality in 1900 was above a third of children dying before age five

intent: A general audience wants the size of the change and why it happened.
goal: The viewer knows the two numbers, why the first was so low, and what raised it.
promise: A line that more than doubles in a century.
arc: A starting point at 32, the children behind it, the line climbing, landing above 70.

events.text: In 1900, a newborn could expect to live about thirty-two years, on average worldwide.
That average was dragged down by children: more than one in three died before age five.
events.knows: More than a third of children died before five.
events.look: the share of children who died young

events.text: Then vaccines, clean water and antibiotics arrived.

demo.what: the line climbing over the century

phases.why: the century passes quickly as the line climbs

events.text: Today it's over seventy. The line more than doubled in a little over a century.

reveal.what: the end of the line above 70

holds.does: the line rests above 70, the gap from 32 marked

quiz.a: Many children died young: more than one in three before age five.

quiz.q: What three things does the clip credit for the rise?
How did the line on the chart move between 1900 and today?
quiz.a: It climbed, more than doubling from about 32 to above 70.

quiz.q: According to the data, how long could a newborn expect to live in 1900 compared with today?
